# Road traffic estimates in Great Britain, 2025: Traffic in Great Britain by road type 

Updated 30 September 2026

## Applies to England, Scotland and Wales 

 Where we have identified any third party copyright information you will need to obtain permission from the copyright holders concerned. 

 This publication is available at https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/road-traffic-estimates-in-great-britain-2025/road-traffic-estimates-in-great-britain-2025-traffic-in-great-britain-by-road-type 

## About this release

This release presents the 2025 annual estimates of traffic on Great Britain’s roads broken down by road type.

Please see the companion releases for a an overview of the 2025 traffic estimates, a breakdown by vehicle type, a breakdown for England’s road networks.

Annual traffic statistics are compiled using data from around 7,000 roadside 12-hour manual counts, continuous data from automatic traffic counters, and data on road lengths. Please see our background quality report for more details.

The next annual traffic statistics release is expected to be published in May 2027, reporting 2026 traffic figures.

This publication includes both accredited official statistics [footnote 1] and official statistics. For more information, see the background information section.

## Overview

In 2025, all road types saw an increase in traffic levels compared to the previous year, and all road types were above 2019 pre-pandemic traffic levels.

Chart 28: Vehicle miles travelled by road type in Great Britain, 2019 to 2025

Chart 28 is a bar chart that shows that traffic levels for motorways increased by 2.4% between 2024 and 2025, and were 2.0% above the 2019 pre-pandemic levels.

Traffic on ‘A’ roads rose 1.9% between 2024 and 2025. ‘A’ road traffic in 2025 was 0.9% above pre-pandemic 2019 levels.

Minor road traffic levels increased by 1.5% between 2024 and 2025, and in 2025 were 1.0% above pre-pandemic 2019 levels.

Chart 29: Share of traffic and length by road types in Great Britain, 2025

Chart 29 is a bar chart that shows that vehicle activity is unevenly distributed across Great Britain’s road network. In 2025, 65% of the motor vehicle miles travelled were on motorways and ‘A’ roads, despite comprising only 13% of the road network by length.

Chart 30: Number of vehicles passing per 24 hours on a typical stretch of road, 2025

Chart 30 is a bar chart that shows that, on an average day in 2025, 56 times more vehicles travelled along a typical stretch of motorway than a typical stretch of a minor road (‘B’ roads, ‘C’ roads, and unclassified roads).

## Motorway traffic

Motorways

Includes major roads of regional and urban strategic importance, often used for long distance travel. They are usually 3 or more lanes in each direction and generally have the maximum speed limit of 70mph.

In 2025, 71.9 billion vehicle miles were travelled on Great Britain’s motorways, an increase of 2.4% on the 2024 total. Motorway traffic in 2025 was higher than 2019 pre-pandemic levels (+2.0%).

Chart 31: Motorway miles in Great Britain, 2015 to 2025

Chart 31 is a bar chart that shows that motor vehicle miles travelled on motorways in Great Britain saw year-on-year growth in each year between 2015 and 2019. This was followed by a sharp decline in 2020 and then increases in the following years. Traffic levels between 2024 and 2025 increased by 2.4%. 2025 levels are 2.0% higher when compared to the 2019 pre-pandemic levels.

Chart 32: Motorway miles by vehicle type in Great Britain, 2019 to 2025

Chart 32 is a bar chart that shows that traffic levels on motorways for cars and other vehicles increased between 2024 and 2025, while traffic for vans and lorries decreased.

Between 2024 and 2025:

- car traffic increased by 4.1% on Great Britain’s motorways to 50.8 billion vehicle miles
- van traffic fell by 1.2% to 13.0 billion vehicle miles
- lorry traffic fell 2.0% to 7.7 billion vehicle miles
- other vehicles (motorcycles and buses and coaches) traffic levels increased by 7.3%

Compared to 2019 motorway traffic levels, in 2025 traffic levels for lorries and other vehicles remain below pre-pandemic levels, whereas vans had traffic above pre-pandemic levels, and cars had traffic levels that were broadly similar to 2019.

Motorways are generally the busiest roads. The busiest road sections tend to be similar each year. This year’s 5 busiest road sections are the same as 2024, with the 4th and 5th road sections switched. The road link with the highest average daily traffic flows in 2025 was a section of the M25.

5 busiest road sections

Vehicles per day in 2025 (rounded figures)

1. M25 - junction 14 to 15: 213,000

2. M25 - junction 13 to 14: 210,000

3. M25 - junction 15 to 16: 209,000

4. M60 - junction 12 to 13: 201,000

5. M25 - junction 12 to 13: 193,000

## ‘A’ road traffic

‘A’ Roads

Includes both principal and trunk ‘A’ roads. They are often described as the ‘main’ roads and tend to have heavy traffic flows, though not as high as motorways.

In 2025, 151.6 billion vehicle miles were travelled on Great Britain’s ‘A’ roads, an increase of 1.9% on the 2024 total. Compared to 2019, ‘A’ road traffic was 0.9% higher in 2025.

Chart 33: ‘A’ road miles in Great Britain, 2015 to 2025

Chart 33 is a bar chart that shows that motor vehicle miles travelled on ‘A’ roads in Great Britain saw year-on-year growth in each year between 2015 and 2019. This was followed by a sharp decline in 2020 and then increases in the following years. Traffic levels between 2024 and 2025 increased by 1.9% on Britain’s A’ roads.

Chart 34: ‘A’ road miles by vehicle type in Great Britain, 2019 to 2025

Chart 34 is a bar chart that shows that traffic levels on ‘A’ roads increased for cars, vans and other vehicles between 2024 and 2025, while traffic for lorries decreased.

Between 2024 and 2025:

- car traffic increased by 2.4% on Great Britain’s ‘A’ roads to 117.1 billion vehicle miles
- van traffic rose 1.0% to 25.0 billion vehicle miles
- lorry traffic fell 1.9% to 7.3 billion vehicle miles
- other vehicles increased by 2.7%

Compared to pre-pandemic 2019 levels, 2025 traffic for cars, lorries and other vehicles remained below pre-pandemic levels, whereas traffic for vans was above 2019 levels.

## Minor road traffic

Minor Roads

Includes ‘B’ and ‘C’ classified roads and unclassified roads (all of which are maintained by local authorities). Private roads are not included.

In 2025, 119.0 billion vehicle miles were travelled on Great Britain’s minor roads, an increase of 1.5% on the 2024 total. Compared to 2019, minor road traffic was 1.0% higher in 2025.

Chart 35: Minor road miles in Great Britain, 2015 to 2025

Chart 35 is a bar chart that shows that motor vehicle miles travelled on minor roads in Great Britain generally saw year-on-year growth in each year between 2015 and 2019. This was followed by a sharp decline in 2020 and then increases in the years since. Traffic levels on minor roads in 2025 were 1.5% above 2024.

Chart 36: Minor road miles by vehicle type in Great Britain, 2019 to 2025

Chart 36 is a bar chart that shows that traffic levels on Great Britain’s minor roads increased for cars, vans, lorries, and other vehicles between 2024 and 2025.

Between 2024 and 2025:

- car traffic on minor roads increased by 1.7% to 94.4 billion vehicle miles
- van traffic increased by 0.9% to 20.8 billion vehicle miles
- lorry traffic on minor roads increased by 2.0% to 1.3 billion vehicle miles
- other vehicles saw a 1.0% rise

Compared to pre-pandemic 2019 levels, 2025 traffic on Great Britain’s minor roads for lorries remained lower. Traffic levels for cars, vans and other vehicles were higher than 2019.

## Background information

Annual estimates make use of data from around 8,000 manual traffic counts in addition to continuous data from a national network of automatic traffic counters (ATCs). These data sources produce accurate estimates on traffic levels in Great Britain by vehicle type and by road type.

This publication is a compendium of both accredited official statistics [footnote 1] and official statistics. The type of statistics presented is detailed below.

- Accredited Official Statistics: National and regional road traffic estimates and flow estimates

(Datasets: TRA0101-TRA0106, TRA0202-TRA0206, TRA0301-TRA0303, TRA0401-TRA0413, TRA3105, TRA4101-TRA4116, TRA4201-TRA4216.)

These official statistics were independently reviewed by the Office for Statistics Regulation in February 2013. They comply with the standards of trustworthiness, quality and value in the Code of Practice for Statistics and should be labelled ‘accredited official statistics’.

- Other official statistics: Temporal road traffic estimates

(Datasets: TRA0305-TRA0308.)

Traffic temporal distributions are not as robust, as they are based on only the ATC data, and must be treated with caution. These statistics are official statistics. They comply with the standards of trustworthiness, quality, and value in the Code of Practice for Statistics.

- Other official statistics: Static road network road traffic estimates

(Datasets: TRA4201-TRA4216)

Traffic estimates based on a static road management status were developed after the last review of these statistics. These statistics are official statistics. They comply with the standards of trustworthiness, quality, and value in the Code of Practice for Statistics.

- Other official statistics: Local authority road traffic estimates

(Datasets: TRA8901-TRA8907)

Traffic at this level is not as robust, due to the sample size of the minor road data, and must be treated with caution. These statistics are official statistics. They comply with the standards of trustworthiness, quality, and value in the Code of Practice for Statistics.

Further information about these statistics is available, including:

- a detailed explanation of the methodology used to produce DfT road traffic statistics can be found online in the annual road traffic estimates: background quality report
- notes and definitions for the road traffic statistics
- the data tables, which give further detail of the key results presented in this statistical release
- a geographical website that allows users to view and download estimated traffic flows on every link of the ‘A’ road and motorway network in Great Britain

Details of Ministers and officials who receive pre-release access to these statistics up to 24 hours before release can be found on the pre-release access page.

## Instructions for printing and saving

Depending on which browser you use and the type of device you use (such as a mobile or laptop) these instructions may vary.

You will find your print and save options in your browser’s menu. You may also have other options available on your device. Tablets and mobile device instructions will be specific to the make and model of the device.

## How to search

Select Ctrl and F on a Windows laptop or Command and F on a Mac

This will open a search box in the top right-hand corner of the page. Type the word you are looking for in the search bar and press enter.
